newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker on strong jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker on strong jobs data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Friday as strong Canadian and U.S. employment reports increased expectations that interest rates would rise, analysts said.

"All the demand indicators are strong for Canada and that's putting pressure on the front end of our bonds. That was exacerbated by the U.S. report," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "It's increased the odds of a (U.S. rate) move."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.13 to C$112.25 to yield 7.015 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.90 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 13 basis points on Thursday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets weakened after the U.S. Labor Department reported that 138,000 jobs were created in May and that the unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent. While the number of new jobs was lower than expected, upward revisions to the jobs data for the previous two months worried many investors, as did the drop in the unemployment rate. The data increased concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee would hike rates in July.
In Canada, Statistics Canada reported that employment rose by 61,300 jobs in May, well above expectations of a 34,700 increase. The unemployment rate fell to 9.5 percent from 9.6 percent in April.
"Canada's number was unequivocably strong. We've had very good growth now for three months," said Goldman's Chandler. "That follows very strong domestic demand numbers in the first quarter."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.24 to C$105.32 to yield 6.515 percent, while the U.S. 10-year fell 6/32 to 6.64 percent.
The negative spread narrowed to 13 basis points from 14 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.93 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.11 percent.
